versions.changelog:
- Minor documentation restructure and naming update in SKILL.md for clarity and consistency.
- Renamed interfaces to skill-docker:interface-01, skill-docker:interface-02, etc.
- Streamlined and reformatted usage steps and interface descriptions.
- Removed the skill-card.md file.
- No changes to command functionality or logic.

- Clarified modification policy: Added an "Important Principles" section emphasizing that files under skill-docker must not be edited directly.
- No functional or interface changes to the skill itself.
- Documentation was restructured for clearer guidance regarding maintenance and file integrity.

- Documentation updated: new warning not to modify any files under skill-docker.
- No functional or interface changes.

- Documentation updated to clarify that DOCKER_BUILDER_NAME is now prompted only if not provided during build and push.
- Step 4.1 in docker:interface 4 now checks if DOCKER_BUILDER_NAME is available before prompting the user.
- Added more explicit step descriptions for user prompts and variable assignment in the build and push workflow.
- Minor formatting and consistency improvements to interface documentation.

- Renamed script: fixed typo in build destroy script (now scripts/docker_buildx_destroy.sh).
- Updated all documentation and commands to reference the correct script name.
- Improved environment variable names for clarity and consistency throughout the usage instructions.
- Clarified input and output specifications for all interfaces.
- Expanded and refined step-by-step instructions for the build and push workflow.

- Added three new scripts: docker_buildx_init.sh, docker_buildx_destory.sh, and docker_buildx_push.sh.
- Introduced new interfaces for builder initialization, destruction, and image build & push using Buildx.
- Updated documentation with detailed usage instructions and expected outputs for each script.
- Expanded functionality beyond manifest inspect to cover the full build and push workflow.

Initial release of skill-docker.

- Adds interface to inspect Docker image manifests via a shell script.
- Accepts a Docker image and one or more tags as input.
- Returns JSON with tag existence and architecture details on success.
- Provides clear error messages for usage and authentication issues.
